targets.authors: Salsbury, T., S. A. Crossley & D. S. McNamara
targets.title: Psycholinguistic word information in second language oral discourse.
targets.evidence_quote: The purpose of this study was to provide an approximate or partial replication of Salsbury et al. (2011), who examined the longitudinal growth of lexical features related to core lexical items (i.e., word concreteness, imageability, familiarity, and meaningfulness).
targets.outcome_quote: This replication study addresses these areas and the findings from the replication fully support those reported by Salsbury et al. providing strong support for the notion that developing L2 lexicons move from the production of words with stronger links to core lexical items to words with weaker links to core lexical items over time.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall verdict of full support; discussion confirms all four central lexical features agree, including the null familiarity result.
